prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Rates & Fed.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
2-yr, 10-yr, 30-yr Treasury yields (level, bp change); Treasury auction results (high yield, bid-to-cover, tail); CME FedWatch probabilities for the next FOMC; every Fed official who spoke, with verbatim quotes.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Rates & Fed `[Macro]`

- The **2-year Treasury yield** was **4.797%**, down **2 bp**, at approximately **08:16 ET on Monday, October 5**. (CNBC, Oct 5 08:16 ET)
- The **10-year Treasury yield** was **5.255%**, down **more than 1 bp**, at approximately **08:16 ET on Monday, October 5**. (CNBC, Oct 5 08:16 ET)
- The **30-year Treasury yield** was **5.614%**, down **1 bp**, at approximately **08:16 ET on Monday, October 5**. (CNBC, Oct 5 08:16 ET)
- On Friday, October 2, the **2-year yield** closed at **4.718%**, down **6.86 bp**; the **10-year yield** closed at **5.178%**, down **5.6 bp**; and the **30-year yield** closed at **5.5704%**, down **3.26 bp**. (Reuters, Oct 2; republished Oct 4 19:00 ET)
- The **2s10s spread** was approximately **+46 bp** on Friday, October 2. (Reuters, Oct 2; republished Oct 4 19:00 ET)
- CME FedWatch indicated an approximately **82% probability that the Fed would leave rates unchanged** at its next meeting as of Monday morning, October 5. (CNBC, Oct 5 08:16 ET)
- Chicago Fed President **Austan Goolsbee** said on Friday, October 2: “There is plenty of room for anything to be on the table,” when asked whether the Fed should raise rates or pause in October. (Reuters, Oct 2)
- Goolsbee also said: “Let’s see if we can get some evidence put together that suggests we’re headed back to 2% inflation.” (Reuters, Oct 2)
- New York Fed President **John Williams** said: “Given the policy decision we made at our September meeting, there is no urgent need to act and we have time to gather more information.” (Reuters, published Oct 5)
- Williams said the Fed could wait for more data while still expecting **one additional rate increase before year-end**. (Reuters, published Oct 5)
- Fed Vice Chair **Philip Jefferson** said: “My colleagues and I will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time.” (Reuters, published Oct 5)
- Jefferson said future policy adjustments should be determined by “carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance…” (Reuters, published Oct 5)
- Dallas Fed President **Lorie Logan** said rates may need to rise by an additional **50 bp or more**. (Saxo Bank, Oct 5 10:18 ET)
- Fed Vice Chair for Supervision **Michelle Bowman** signaled that there was **no urgent need for further rate action**. (Saxo Bank, Oct 5 10:18 ET)
- The next FOMC meeting was scheduled for **October 27–28**, with the policy announcement due at **14:00 ET on Wednesday, October 28**. (OpenBook Analytics, Oct 2 18:54 ET)

## Treasury Auctions `[Macro]`

- The available October 2 auction result was for **Japan’s Treasury discount bills**, not a U.S. Treasury auction: **¥11,710.50 billion** in competitive bids were submitted against **¥2,698.48 billion** accepted, with a lowest accepted yield of **1.2875%**. (Japan Ministry of Finance, Oct 2)
- No U.S. Treasury coupon-auction result with a high yield, bid-to-cover ratio, and tail was identified in the available search results for the October 2–October 5 12:20 ET window.
